one_liner: Hand-unrolled FP32 CUDA kernels for L_max=3 spherical harmonics and Clebsch-Gordan tensor products, timed against generic e3nn.
what_it_does: A PyTorch C++/CUDA extension with the inner operations of equivariant interatomic potentials (MACE, NequIP, Allegro): real spherical harmonics of edge vectors, CG tensor products (unweighted, or with per-path C_in x C_out weights), a fused SH+TP message kernel and CSR message passing. It is not a drop-in for e3nn modules: you call plain functions on fixed layouts (node features [N, C, 16], Y_lm [N, 16], weights [34, C_in, C_out]), and torch.autograd.Function wrappers in batmobile/autograd.py call hand-written backward kernels.
how_it_is_fast: For L_max=3 all 34 CG paths and their 611 non-zero coefficients are generated as compile-time constants (scripts/gen_fused_tp.py, cg_coefficients_l3.cuh) and fully unrolled, so no sparse CG tables are read and no per-path kernel launches happen. The weighted kernel gives each (sample, output channel) pair a thread block that accumulates in shared memory. The fused SH+TP kernel computes the 16 harmonics in registers from closed-form polynomials and uses them right away, so Y_lm never goes to global memory.
when_to_use: Custom MACE/NequIP-style models on Ampere consumer GPUs (built for RTX 3090, sm_86) that use exactly L_max=3 irreps 0e+1o+2e+3o in FP32.
Prototyping or studying how fused, unrolled CG kernels beat e3nn's generic einsum/codegen path on small irreps.
Spherical harmonics alone for L_max 0-6 on unit vectors, where the SH kernel gave 11.8x over e3nn at 1,000 edges in the README.
Workloads whose bottleneck is the unweighted SH x feature product per edge, where the fused kernel avoids materializing Y_lm.
when_not_to_use: Production MD runs: 3 commits, no releases, no CI, and the package does not import at HEAD (see gotchas).
Any L_max other than 3 for tensor products; the binding checks that inputs have exactly 16 components.
FP64 or mixed-precision simulations: every binding requires float32 (the README says FP32 only, no FP64).
GPUs other than sm_86-compatible: setup.py builds SASS only for compute_86/sm_86 with no PTX, so A100 (sm_80) and Hopper/Blackwell need the flag edited.
If you need a vetted fast equivariant backend: issues #1 and #3 point to OpenEquivariance and NVIDIA cuEquivariance, and batmobile has not been benchmarked against either.

integration.dependencies: PyTorch >=2.0, NumPy >=1.20, CUDA toolkit, pybind11 (via torch.utils.cpp_extension); e3nn, torch_scatter and torch_cluster for tests/benchmarks
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (g++ and nvcc -std=c++17); CUDA 12.x per README (LLMS.txt says 11.8+); Python >=3.9
integration.platforms: NVIDIA sm_86 as shipped (RTX 3090 / RTX 30xx); other archs need TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST and the hard-coded -gencode flag in setup.py changed; Linux assumed, others not documented

gotchas: Broken import at HEAD: commit e4fa3a9 'Rename project from batteries to batmobile' renamed the built module to '_batmobile' (setup.py, bindings.cpp, autograd.py), but python/batmobile/__init__.py and every benchmark/test script still do 'import _batteries', so 'import batmobile' and the README benchmark commands fail until patched; benchmark_e2e_mace.py also imports a nonexistent 'python.autograd'.
The README autograd example imports SphericalHarmonics and TensorProduct from batmobile.autograd, but that module defines SphericalHarmonicsFunction, TensorProductFunction and lowercase wrappers.

The tensor-product speedup is not equal work: tests/benchmark_tensor_product.py times the unweighted tensor_product_simple, which sums paths into 16 outputs (l <= 3), against e3nn o3.FullTensorProduct, which outputs every (l1, l2) -> l path up to l=6; the weighted, channelled kernel has no e3nn timing ('too slow for direct comparison').
spherical_harmonics expects already-normalized vectors (docstring: 'must be normalized'); the benchmark calls e3nn with normalize=False to match.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No equivariant-GNN sibling is catalogued yet; the nearest siblings (tiny-cuda-nn's fully fused MLPs, Liger-Kernel's fused PyTorch ops) target other layers, so batmobile is only worth considering as a readable reference for fused L_max=3 SH/CG kernels, not as a replacement for them.
verified_claims_summary: Single-author timings on one RTX 3090 (CUDA 12.x, PyTorch 2.x, -O3 --use_fast_math, host CPU not stated) at 1,000 atoms, C=32, about 20 neighbours: SH 0.012 ms vs e3nn 0.142 ms (11.8x, CUDA-event timed), unweighted TP 20.8x and TP backward 20.6x over e3nn, while the 1.39x 'Fused SH+TP' row and the 1.45x at-scale row compare fused against batmobile's own unfused pipeline. The TP comparison does less work than e3nn's FullTensorProduct, and the scripts cannot run at HEAD without fixing the module name.
status_note: MIT-licensed, 44 stars, all 3 commits on 2026-01-17 (co-authored with an AI assistant), and three open issues with no maintainer replies; small enough to vendor and study, but it needs a one-line import fix and an arch-flag edit before it builds and runs anywhere but an RTX 30xx.
